title: Wave planner can re-pick a scope whose inbox item is already consumed — one confirmed instance (cycle-1116)
notes: Evidence CORRECTED after adversarial fact-check (2026-07-27, batch-12 attempt-3) — earlier draft overstated the waste. Actual history of scope tdd-topn-binding-gate: 1103 = triage stale-drop no-op PASS (empty top_n); 1106/1107/1109/1111 = a legitimate multi-cycle refinement chain under the same goal-derived LANE LABEL but with distinct per-cycle tasks (topngate-authored-file-scope-check FAIL, archive task FAIL, empty-top_n PASS, real gate.go change PASS); 1113 = genuine completion + transactional consumption to .evolve/inbox/processed/cycle-1113/. The ONE confirmed defect instance: cycle-1116's lane-scope.json re-pins todo_ids=[tdd-topn-binding-gate] AFTER the item was consumed at 1113 — the planner's scope source (carryoverTodos/goal seed) has no consumed-item freshness check at plan time. Fix shape: when seeding a wave plan, drop todo ids that resolve to .evolve/inbox/processed/ (see inboxmover promoteDestPath semantics; freshness probe lives in cmd_loop_wave.go productionFreshnessProbe/seedWavePlanFromInbox, ~lines 259-355/445-500) unless a NEW inbox item or a FAIL-continuation stamp re-names them; single serialized state RMW, no second bookkeeping file. Regression: planner plan for wave N+1 must exclude a scope consumed at wave N; pin with a two-wave fixture. GOTCHA for future triage: lane LABELS are goal-derived and repeat across waves — always read the per-cycle build-report task line before diagnosing re-pick waste.
